summary: Frontend-only testing of SINGLE global river requirement on cGreen landing page (desktop 1440x900). Verified exactly one [data-testid=global-river] element exists at all scroll positions (top, 15/30/45/60/75/90/100%, back up to top). Anchors (urban/rural/logo) present. River originates at bottom of urban circle, weaves through rural circle (with circle-hole mask for morph), and terminates at cGreen logo. Two lanes of dark forest-green digits (#4C7E5B and #3C6A4B) — muted, not neon. No duplicate river fragments visible at any scroll position. Reversibility verified. Regression: contact section, hero orbit (543 descendants), and page structure OK.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: Framer-motion console warning 'You have defined a target options but the provided ref is not yet hydrated' appears twice on load — non-blocking but should be silenced by moving useScroll() closer to the ref or setting layoutEffect:false.

The GlobalRiver SVG is present in DOM even before hero captions finish (progress=0 keeps it invisible via mask). This satisfies 'not visible yet' but if strict DOM absence is desired, gate the render on `ready` too.
Regression check for service-tab data-testid found 0 elements — the services tabs may use a different selector prefix. Confirm data-testid naming for future tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: SINGLE-river bug is FIXED. Verified via document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=global-river]').length === 1 at all scroll positions on desktop 1440x900. Screenshots confirm continuous weaving path from urban circle -> rural circle -> cGreen logo with muted dark-green digits. Mobile intentionally has no river (isDesktop gate).
rca of the issue: Previous duplicate-river bug resolved by consolidating all per-section river components into a single page-level GlobalRiver instance rendered once in CGreenLanding.jsx, measuring absolute page coordinates of urban/rural/logo anchors and drawing one continuous SVG path with a scroll-driven mask reveal.
